    "source": "README_FOR_MARKETPLACE_277C.md",
    "content": "# PowerShell  for Azure Data Studio\n\n[![Build Status](https://dev.azure.com/powershell/vscode-powershell/_apis/build/status/PowerShell.vscode-powershell?branchName=main)](https://dev.azure.com/powershell/vscode-powershell/_build/latest?definitionId=51&branchName=main)\n[![Version](https://vsmarketplacebadge.apphb.com/version/ms-vscode.PowerShell.svg)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.PowerShell)\n[![Installs](https://vsmarketplacebadge.apphb.com/installs-short/ms-vscode.PowerShell.svg)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.PowerShell)\n[![Join the chat on Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/180528040881815552.svg?label=%23vscode&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://aka.ms/powershell-vscode-discord)\n[![Join the chat on Gitter](https://badges.gitter.im/PowerShell/vscode-powershell.svg)](https://gitter.im/PowerShell/vscode-powershell?utm_source=badge&utm_medium=badge&utm_campaign=pr-badge&utm_content=badge)\n\nThis extension provides rich PowerShell language support for [Azure Data Studio](https://github.com/Microsoft/azuredatastudio) (ADS).\nNow you can write and run PowerShell scripts using the excellent IDE-like interface\nthat ADS provides.\n\nThis extension is powered by the PowerShell language server,\n[PowerShell Editor Services](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShellEditorServices).\nThis leverages the\n[Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/)\nwhere `PowerShellEditorServices` is the server and `vscode-powershell` is the client.\n\nAlso included in this extension is the PowerShell ISE theme for Visual Studio Code. It is\nnot activated by default, but after installing this extension either click \"Set Color\nTheme\" or use the [theme picker](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/themes) and\nselect \"PowerShell ISE\" for a fun and familiar experience.\n\n## Platform Support\n\nThe extension _should_ work anywhere ADS itself and PowerShell Core 7.2 or higher is\n[supported][]. For Windows PowerShell, only version 5.1 is supported. Please note that\nPowerShell Core 6 is end-of-life and so not supported. Our test matrix includes the\nfollowing:\n\n- **Windows Server 2022** with Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell Core 7.2.7\n- **Windows Server 2019** with Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell Core 7.2.7\n- **macOS 11** with PowerShell Core 7.2.7\n- **Ubuntu 20.04** with PowerShell Core 7.2.7\n\n[supported]: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/powershell-support-lifecycle?view=powershell-7.1#supported-platforms\n\nRead the [installation instructions](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/components/vscode/using-vscode)\nto get more details on how to use the extension on these platforms.\n\n**Read the [troubleshooting guide](./docs/troubleshooting.md) for answers to common questions.**\n\n## Features\n\n- Syntax highlighting\n- Code snippets\n- IntelliSense for cmdlets and more\n- Rule-based analysis provided by [PowerShell Script Analyzer](http://github.com/PowerShell/PSScriptAnalyzer)\n- Go to Definition of cmdlets and variables\n- Find References of cmdlets and variables\n- Document and workspace symbol discovery\n- Run selected selection of PowerShell code using <kbd>F8</kbd>\n- Launch online help for the symbol under the cursor using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F1</kbd>\n- Local script debugging\n- Extension Terminal support\n- PowerShell ISE color theme\n\n## Installing the Extension\n\nYou can install the official release of the PowerShell extension by following the steps\nin the [Azure Data Studio documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/azure-data-studio/extensions).\nIn the Extensions pane, search for \"PowerShell\" extension and install it there.  You will\nget notified automatically about any future extension updates!\n\nYou can also install a VSIX package from our [releases page](https://github.com/PowerShell/vscode-powershell/releases) by following the\n[Install from a VSIX](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/extension-gallery#_install-from-a-vsix)\ninstructions. The easiest way is through the command line:\n\n```powershell\nazuredatastudio --install-extension powershell-<version>.vsix\n```\n\n## Reporting Problems\n\nIf you experience any problems with the PowerShell Extension, see\n[the troubleshooting docs](./docs/troubleshooting.md) for information\non diagnosing and reporting issues.\n\n## Security Note\n\nFor any security issues, please see [here](./SECURITY.md).\n\n## Example Scripts\n\nThere are some example scripts in the extension's `examples` folder that you can\nuse to discover PowerShell editing and debugging functionality.  Please\ncheck out the included [README.md](examples/README.md) file to learn more about\nhow to use them.\n\nThis folder can be found at the following path:\n\n```powershell\n$HOME/.azuredatastudio/extensions/ms-vscode.powershell-<version>/examples\n```\n\nTo open/view the extension's examples in Azure Data Studio, run the following from your\nPowerShell session:\n\n```powershell\nazuredatastudio (Get-Chil"

PRESENTACIÃ“N La Navidad es una Ã©poca que nos invita a compartir nuestras tradiciones, costumbres y valores culturales; a recordar la importancia de dar y recibir amor, practicar la solidaridad, alimentar el espÃ­ritu y disfrutar de los pequeÃ±os momentos de la vida. Para muchas personas migrantes, estas fechas evocan sentimientos profundos, especialmente cuando sus seres queridos permanecen en sus paÃ­ses de origen. La Navidad despierta en todos nosotros los mejores sentimientos: paz, armonÃ­a, fraternidad, solidaridad y el valor de la familia y los amigos. Attempting to automatically update now...\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"df376c67-2bb7-42e7-b46d-91c2c48acde3\",\n      \"timestamp\": \"2026-03-25T10:37:41.457Z\",\n      \"type\": \"info\",\n      \"content\": \"Update successful! Pero hoy ya puedes tener un agente de programaciÃ³n funcionando en tu propio ordenador, sin coste y con control total.\\nEn esta guÃ­a vas a aprender a instalar y configurar Claude Code utilizando Ollama, para trabajar con modelos locales sin depender de servicios externos.\\nðŸ§  QuÃ© es Claude Code y por quÃ© importa\\nClaude Code es un agente de programaciÃ³n que funciona desde la terminal. No es un simple chat: puede leer archivos, escribir cÃ³digo, modificar proyectos completos y ayudarte a automatizar tareas reales.\\nLa clave es que trabaja directamente sobre tu entorno, lo que lo hace mucho mÃ¡s potente que usar IA en navegador.\\nâš™ï¸ QuÃ© es Ollama\\nOllama te permite ejecutar modelos de IA en local, en tu propio ordenador. No necesitas pagar por uso ni enviar datos fuera.\\nAdemÃ¡s, instalar y cambiar modelos es tan simple como ejecutar un comando.\\nðŸ§© Requisitos antes de empezar\\nNecesitas un ordenador con suficiente capacidad (especialmente RAM), acceso a terminal y conexiÃ³n a internet para descargar los modelos.\\nðŸ§± InstalaciÃ³n de Ollama\\nInstala Ollama desde su web oficial: https://ollama.com/download \\n\\n\\n\\n\\nðŸ¤– Descargar modelos en Ollama\\nPuedes explorar modelos disponibles aquÃ­:\\nhttps://ollama.com/search\\nPara instalar cualquiera, usa:\\nollama pull nombre-del-modelo\\nPor ejemplo:\\nollama pull qwen3.5:0.8b\\nEsto deja el modelo preparado en local para usarlo cuando quieras.\\nðŸ§± InstalaciÃ³n de Claude Code\\nAhoraâ€¦\\nðŸ Instala Claude Code si tienes Mac con:\\ncurl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash\\nðŸªŸ Instala Claude Code si tienes Windows con:\\nirm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex\\nEsto aÃ±adirÃ¡ el comando claude a tu sistema.\\nðŸ’¡ Pro tip: Si te da error prueba hacerlo desde el terminal de Antigravity, compartir los errores con el agente y asÃ­ lo podrÃ¡ solventar por tÃ­\\nðŸ”— Conectar Claude Code con Ollama\\nPor defecto Claude Code usa la API de Anthropic (de pago). AquÃ­ lo redirigimos a Ollama.\\nConfigura estas variables:\\nexport ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama\\nexport ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434\\nCon esto, Claude Code usarÃ¡ modelos locales (AquÃ­ no hace falta hacer nada,es solo informativo).\\nðŸš€ Ejecutar Claude Code\\nPuedes iniciarlo simplemente con:\\nollama launch claude\\n\\n\\n\\nO lanzarlo con un modelo concreto:\\nollama launch claude --model qwen3.5:0.8b\\nYa tienes el agente funcionando en local.\\n\\nðŸ” Comprobar que todo estÃ¡ correcto\\nDentro de Claude Code ejecuta:\\n/model\\nSi aparece un modelo local, estÃ¡ bien configurado.\\n\\nâš¡ QuÃ© puedes hacer con esto\\nPuedes crear aplicaciones, revisar cÃ³digo, automatizar tareas o trabajar directamente sobre proyectos reales.\\nTambiÃ©n puedes usar comandos como /loop para automatizar procesos y convertirlo en un agente mÃ¡s autÃ³nomo.\\nAquÃ­ no solo estÃ¡s instalando una herramienta.     "source": "SKILL_8EE1.md",
    "content": "---\nname: troubleshoot\ndescription: Investigate unexpected chat agent behavior by analyzing direct debug logs in JSONL files. Use when users ask why something happened, why a request was slow, why tools or subagents were used or skipped, or why instructions/skills/agents did not load.\n---\n\n# Troubleshoot\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis skill investigates and explains unexpected chat agent behavior using direct log files.\n\nUse this skill for questions like:\n- Why did this request take so long?\n- Why was a tool or subagent called?\n- Why did instruction/skill/agent files not load?\n- Why was a tool call blocked or failed?\n- Why did the model not follow expectations?\n\nBase conclusions on evidence from logs. Do not guess.\n\n## Data Source\n\n{{DEBUG_LOG_RUNTIME_CONTEXT}}\n\nUse direct debug log files written by Copilot Chat:\n\n```\ndebug-logs/<sessionId>/\n  main.jsonl                              â€” always start here; primary conversation log\n  runSubagent-<agentName>-<uuid>.jsonl    â€” (optional) subagent's tool calls & LLM requests\n  searchSubagent-<uuid>.jsonl             â€” (optional) search subagent work\n  title-<uuid>.jsonl                      â€” (optional, UI-only) title generation\n  categorization-<uuid>.jsonl             â€” (optional, UI-only) prompt categorization\n  summarize-<uuid>.jsonl                  â€” (optional, UI-only) conversation summarization\n```\n\nAlways read `main.jsonl` first â€” it has the full conversation flow. Child files only appear when those operations occurred. `main.jsonl` contains `child_session_ref` entries that link to each child file by name. Title, categorization, and summarize files are UI housekeeping and rarely relevant to troubleshooting.\n\nEach line is a JSON object. Common fields: `ts` (epoch ms), `dur` (duration ms), `sid` (session ID), `type`, `name`, `spanId`, `parentSpanId`, `status` (`ok`|`error`), `attrs` (type-specific details).\n\n### Event Type Reference with Examples\n\n#### discovery â€” customization file loading (instructions, skills, agents, hooks)\n```jsonl\n{\"ts\":1773200251309,\"dur\":0,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"discovery\",\"name\":\"Load Instructions\",\"spanId\":\"2cb1f2f4\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"details\":\"Resolved 0 instructions in 0.0ms | folders: [/c:/Users/user/.copilot/instructions, /workspace/.github/instructions]\",\"category\":\"discovery\",\"source\":\"core\"}}\n{\"ts\":1773200251415,\"dur\":0,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"discovery\",\"name\":\"Load Agents\",\"spanId\":\"38a897d8\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"details\":\"Resolved 3 agents in 0.0ms | loaded: [Plan, Ask, Explore] | folders: [/workspace/.github/agents]\",\"category\":\"discovery\",\"source\":\"core\"}}\n{\"ts\":1773200251431,\"dur\":0,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"discovery\",\"name\":\"Load Skills\",\"spanId\":\"472eb225\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"details\":\"Resolved 6 skills in 0.0ms | loaded: [agent-customization, troubleshoot, ...]\",\"category\":\"discovery\",\"source\":\"core\"}}\n```\nKey attrs: `details` (human-readable summary with folder paths, loaded items, skip reasons), `category` (always `\"discovery\"`), `source` (`\"core\"`).\n\n#### tool_call â€” tool invocation (success or failure)\n```jsonl\n{\"ts\":1773200222647,\"dur\":4,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"manage_todo_list\",\"spanId\":\"000000000000000b\",\"parentSpanId\":\"0000000000000003\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"args\":\"{\\\"operation\\\":\\\"read\\\"}\",\"result\":\"No todo list found.\"}}\n{\"ts\":1773200234047,\"dur\":8937,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"run_in_terminal\",\"spanId\":\"000000000000000d\",\"parentSpanId\":\"0000000000000003\",\"status\":\"error\",\"attrs\":{\"args\":\"{\\\"command\\\":\\\"echo rama\\\"}\",\"result\":\"ERROR: conpty.node missing\",\"error\":\"A native exception occurred during launch\"}}\n```\nKey attrs: `args` (JSON string of tool input), `result` (tool output or error text), `error` (present when `status:\"error\"`).\n\n#### llm_request â€” model round-trip\n```jsonl\n{\"ts\":1773200231010,\"dur\":3001,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"llm_request\",\"name\":\"chat:gpt-4o\",\"spanId\":\"000000000000000c\",\"parentSpanId\":\"0000000000000003\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"inputTokens\":15025,\"outputTokens\":126,\"ttft\":1987}}\n```\nKey attrs: `model`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `ttft` (time to first token in ms), `error` (when failed).\n\n#### agent_response â€” model output (text + tool calls)\n```jsonl\n{\"ts\":1773200234011,\"dur\":0,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"agent_response\",\"name\":\"agent_response\",\"spanId\":\"agent-msg-000000000000000c\",\"parentSpanId\":\"0000000000000003\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"response\":\"[{\\\"role\\\":\\\"assistant\\\",\\\"parts\\\":[{\\\"type\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Running your command now.\\\"},{\\\"type\\\":\\\"tool_call\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"run_in_terminal\\\",\\\"arguments\\\":\\\"{...}\\\"}]}]\"}}\n```\nKey attrs: `response` (JSON-encoded array of message parts; may be truncated).\n\n#### user_message â€” user input\n```jsonl\n{\"ts\":1773200251345,\"dur\":0,\"sid\":\"62f52dec\",\"type\":\"user_message\",\"name\":\"user_message\",\"spanId\":\"000000000000000f\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"attrs\":{\"content\":\"using subagent count .md\"}}\n```\nKey attrs: `content` (the user's message text).\n\n#### subagent â€” subagent invocation\n```jsonl\n"

    "source": "SKILL_948E.md",
    "content": "---\nname: build-mcp-app\ndescription: This skill should be used when the user wants to build an \"MCP app\", add \"interactive UI\" or \"widgets\" to an MCP server, \"render components in chat\", build \"MCP UI resources\", make a tool that shows a \"form\", \"picker\", \"dashboard\" or \"confirmation dialog\" inline in the conversation, or mentions \"apps SDK\" in the context of MCP. Use AFTER the build-mcp-server skill has settled the deployment model, or when the user already knows they want UI widgets.\nversion: 0.1.0\n---\n\n# Build an MCP App (Interactive UI Widgets)\n\nAn MCP app is a standard MCP server that **also serves UI resources** â€” interactive components rendered inline in the chat surface. Build once, runs in Claude *and* ChatGPT and any other host that implements the apps surface.\n\nThe UI layer is **additive**. Under the hood it's still tools, resources, and the same wire protocol. If you haven't built a plain MCP server before, the `build-mcp-server` skill covers the base layer. This skill adds widgets on top.\n\n---\n\n## When a widget beats plain text\n\nDon't add UI for its own sake â€” most tools are fine returning text or JSON. Add a widget when one of these is true:\n\n| Signal | Widget type |\n|---|---|\n| Tool needs structured input Claude can't reliably infer | Form |\n| User must pick from a list Claude can't rank (files, contacts, records) | Picker / table |\n| Destructive or billable action needs explicit confirmation | Confirm dialog |\n| Output is spatial or visual (charts, maps, diffs, previews) | Display widget |\n| Long-running job the user wants to watch | Progress / live status |\n\nIf none apply, skip the widget. Text is faster to build and faster for the user.\n\n---\n\n## Widgets vs Elicitation â€” route correctly\n\nBefore building a widget, check if **elicitation** covers it. Elicitation is spec-native, zero UI code, works in any compliant host.\n\n| Need | Elicitation | Widget |\n|---|---|---|\n| Confirm yes/no | âœ… | overkill |\n| Pick from short enum | âœ… | overkill |\n| Fill a flat form (name, email, date) | âœ… | overkill |\n| Pick from a large/searchable list | âŒ (no scroll/search) | âœ… |\n| Visual preview before choosing | âŒ | âœ… |\n| Chart / map / diff view | âŒ | âœ… |\n| Live-updating progress | âŒ | âœ… |\n\nIf elicitation covers it, use it. See `../build-mcp-server/references/elicitation.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture: two deployment shapes\n\n### Remote MCP app (most common)\n\nHosted streamable-HTTP server. Widget templates are served as **resources**; tool results reference them. The host fetches the resource, renders it in an iframe sandbox, and brokers messages between the widget and Claude.\n\n```\nâ”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”  tools/call   â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”\nâ”‚  Claude  â”‚â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> â”‚ MCP server â”‚\nâ”‚   host   â”‚<â”€â”€ result â”€â”€â”€â”€â”‚  (remote)  â”‚\nâ”‚          â”‚  + widget ref â”‚            â”‚\nâ”‚          â”‚               â”‚            â”‚\nâ”‚          â”‚ resources/readâ”‚            â”‚\nâ”‚          â”‚â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> â”‚  widget    â”‚\nâ”‚ â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â” â”‚<â”€â”€ template â”€â”€â”‚  HTML/JS   â”‚\nâ”‚ â”‚iframeâ”‚ â”‚               â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜\nâ”‚ â”‚widgetâ”‚ â”‚\nâ”‚ â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜ â”‚\nâ””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜\n```\n\n### MCPB-packaged MCP app (local + UI)\n\nSame widget mechanism, but the server runs locally inside an MCPB bundle. Use this when the widget needs to drive a **local** application â€” e.g., a file picker that browses the actual local disk, a dialog that controls a desktop app.\n\nFor MCPB packaging mechanics, defer to the **`build-mcpb`** skill. Everything below applies to both shapes.\n\n---\n\n## How widgets attach to tools\n\nA widget-enabled tool has **two separate registrations**:\n\n1. **The tool** declares a UI resource via `_meta.ui.resourceUri`. Its handler returns plain text/JSON â€” NOT the HTML.\n2. **The resource** is registered separately and serves the HTML.\n\nWhen Claude calls the tool, the host sees `_meta.ui.resourceUri`, fetches that resource, renders it in an iframe, and pipes the tool's return value into the iframe via the `ontoolresult` event.\n\n```typescript\nimport { McpServer } from \"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js\";\nimport { registerAppTool, registerAppResource, RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE }\n  from \"@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/server\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nconst server = new McpServer({ name: \"contacts\", version: \"1.0.0\" });\n\n// 1. The tool â€” returns DATA, declares which UI to show\nregisterAppTool(server, \"pick_contact\", {\n  description: \"Open an interactive contact picker\",\n  inputSchema: { filter: z.string().optional() },\n  _meta: { ui: { resourceUri: \"ui://widgets/contact-picker.html\" } },\n}, async ({ filter }) => {\n  const contacts = await db.contacts.search(filter);\n  // Plain JSON â€” the widget receives this via ontoolresult\n  return { content: [{ type: \"text\", text: JSON.stringify(contacts) }] };\n});\n\n// 2. The resource â€” serves the HTML\nregisterAppResource(\n  server,\n  \"Contact Picker\",\n  \"ui://widgets/contact-picker.html\",\n  {},\n  async () => ({\n    contents: [{\n      uri: \"ui://widgets/contact-picker.html\",\n      mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,\n      text: pickerHtml,  // your HTML string\n    }],\n  }),\n);\n`"
  },

    "source": "SKILL_B51F.md",
    "content": "---\nname: ai-seo\ndescription: \"When the user wants to optimize content for AI search engines, get cited by LLMs, or appear in AI-generated answers. Also use when the user mentions 'AI SEO,' 'AEO,' 'GEO,' 'LLMO,' 'answer engine optimization,' 'generative engine optimization,' 'LLM optimization,' 'AI Overviews,' 'optimize for ChatGPT,' 'optimize for Perplexity,' 'AI citations,' 'AI visibility,' 'zero-click search,' 'how do I show up in AI answers,' 'LLM mentions,' or 'optimize for Claude/Gemini.' Use this whenever someone wants their content to be cited or surfaced by AI assistants and AI search engines. For traditional technical and on-page SEO audits, see seo-audit. For structured data implementation, see schema-markup.\"\nmetadata:\n  version: 1.1.0\n---\n\n# AI SEO\n\nYou are an expert in AI search optimization â€” the practice of making content discoverable, extractable, and citable by AI systems including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. Your goal is to help users get their content cited as a source in AI-generated answers.\n\n## Before Starting\n\n**Check for product marketing context first:**\nIf `.agents/product-marketing-context.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing-context.md` in older setups), read it before asking questions. Use that context and only ask for information not already covered or specific to this task.\n\nGather this context (ask if not provided):\n\n### 1. Current AI Visibility\n- Do you know if your brand appears in AI-generated answers today?\n- Have you checked ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Overviews for your key queries?\n- What queries matter most to your business?\n\n### 2. Content & Domain\n- What type of content do you produce? (Blog, docs, comparisons, product pages)\n- What's your domain authority / traditional SEO strength?\n- Do you have existing structured data (schema markup)?\n\n### 3. Goals\n- Get cited as a source in AI answers?\n- Appear in Google AI Overviews for specific queries?\n- Compete with specific brands already getting cited?\n- Optimize existing content or create new AI-optimized content?\n\n### 4. Competitive Landscape\n- Who are your top competitors in AI search results?\n- Are they being cited where you're not?\n\n---\n\n## How AI Search Works\n\n### The AI Search Landscape\n\n| Platform | How It Works | Source Selection |\n|----------|-------------|----------------|\n| **Google AI Overviews** | Summarizes top-ranking pages | Strong correlation with traditional rankings |\n| **ChatGPT (with search)** | Searches web, cites sources | Draws from wider range, not just top-ranked |\n| **Perplexity** | Always cites sources with links | Favors authoritative, recent, well-structured content |\n| **Gemini** | Google's AI assistant | Pulls from Google index + Knowledge Graph |\n| **Copilot** | Bing-powered AI search | Bing index + authoritative sources |\n| **Claude** | Brave Search (when enabled) | Training data + Brave search results |\n\nFor a deep dive on how each platform selects sources and what to optimize per platform, see [references/platform-ranking-factors.md](references/platform-ranking-factors.md).\n\n### Key Difference from Traditional SEO\n\nTraditional SEO gets you ranked. AI SEO gets you **cited**.\n\nIn traditional search, you need to rank on page 1. In AI search, a well-structured page can get cited even if it ranks on page 2 or 3 â€” AI systems select sources based on content quality, structure, and relevance, not just rank position.\n\n**Critical stats:**\n- AI Overviews appear in ~45% of Google searches\n- AI Overviews reduce clicks to websites by up to 58%\n- Brands are 6.5x more likely to be cited via third-party sources than their own domains\n- Optimized content gets cited 3x more often than non-optimized\n- Statistics and citations boost visibility by 40%+ across queries\n\n---\n\n## AI Visibility Audit\n\nBefore optimizing, assess your current AI search presence.\n\n### Step 1: Check AI Answers for Your Key Queries\n\nTest 10-20 of your most important queries across platforms:\n\n| Query | Google AI Overview | ChatGPT | Perplexity | You Cited? | Competitors Cited? |\n|-------|:-----------------:|:-------:|:----------:|:----------:|:-----------------:|\n| [query 1] | Yes/No | Yes/No | Yes/No | Yes/No | [who] |\n| [query 2] | Yes/No | Yes/No | Yes/No | Yes/No | [who] |\n\n**Query types to test:**\n- \"What is [your product category]?\"\n- \"Best [product category] for [use case]\"\n- \"[Your brand] vs [competitor]\"\n- \"How to [problem your product solves]\"\n- \"[Your product category] pricing\"\n\n### Step 2: Analyze Citation Patterns\n\nWhen your competitors get cited and you don't, examine:\n- **Content structure** â€” Is their content more extractable?\n- **Authority signals** â€” Do they have more citations, stats, expert quotes?\n- **Freshness** â€” Is their content more recently updated?\n- **Schema markup** â€” Do they have structured data you're missing?\n- **Third-party presence** â€” Are they cited via Wikipedia, Reddit, review sites?\n\n### Step 3: Content Extractability Check\n\nFor each priority "

(Marketing & Autoridad)  \nWordPress es tu \"Motor de Contenido\" y tu \"Capa de SEO\".\n\nPara quÃ©: Cambiar fotos de bodas, escribir artÃ­culos en el blog sobre eventos en Madrid/Mallorca, gestionar pedidos de WooCommerce (si vendes servicios directos) y ajustar el diseÃ±o visual de las pÃ¡ginas pÃºblicas usando Divi.  \nTu ventaja: Tienes instalados plugins de alto nivel como Rank Math SEO PRO y Divi Machine.
